name: Arizona
notes: This is Arizona's dependent tax credit (A.R.S. 43-1073.01), not a federal-style child tax credit: $125 per dependent under 17 at end of tax year (was $100 before HB 4168, effective tax year 2026) plus $25 per dependent age 17 and older. Credit is reduced by 5% for each $1,000 (or fraction) of federal AGI above $200,000 (single, MFS, head of household) or $400,000 (married filing jointly); there is no fixed income cut-off. Nonresidents and part-year residents prorate by the Arizona income ratio.

name: California
asOf: Tax year 2025 amounts (FTB Young Child Tax Credit page and FTB bill analysis AB 1690, April 2026); tax year 2026 amount not yet published as of 2026-10
notes: Young Child Tax Credit (YCTC) is granted once per tax return, not per child: up to $1,189 for tax year 2025 (base $1,000 indexed for inflation). Requires a CalEITC-qualifying taxpayer with a qualifying child under 6 at year end. Earned income cap $32,900 for tax year 2025 (same for all filing statuses); the credit is reduced by $20 for each $100 of earned income above an indexed threshold ($25,000 statutory base, $26,626 in tax year 2024). The tax year 2026 amount and income thresholds are published by the FTB before the tax year 2026 filing season. AB 1690 (raising the age limit to under 7 for tax year 2026 and up to under 18 by 2038) had not passed as of September 2026, so the age limit for tax year 2026 remains under 6.

name: Colorado
asOf: Tax year 2025 amounts (Colorado DOR Income Tax Topics: Child Tax Credit, revised January 2026); tax year 2026 form DR 0104CN amounts not yet published as of 2026-10
notes: Since tax year 2024 the credit no longer depends on the federal CTC: it is a fixed amount per eligible child under 6 that depends on AGI. Tax year 2025 tiers: single filers $1,200 (AGI $26,000 or less), $600 ($26,001-$51,000), $200 ($51,001-$77,000); joint filers $1,200 ($36,000 or less), $600 ($36,001-$61,000), $200 ($61,001-$87,000). AGI limits: $77,000 single / $87,000 joint (tax year 2025); head of household and married filing separately use the single table. Tax year 2026 tiers are in form DR 0104CN, published before the tax year 2026 filing season. The separate refundable Family Affordability Tax Credit (FATC) is NOT available in tax year 2026 because its revenue trigger is not met (up to $3,273 per child under 6 in tax year 2025). A new Family Affordability Credit from H.B. 1223 starts in tax year 2027.

name: Georgia
asOf: Tax year 2026 (H.B. 136 (2025), O.C.G.A. 48-7-29.27, signed 2025-05-13; Georgia DOR Qualifying Child Credit page)
notes: New credit first available for tax year 2026: $250 per qualifying child (same meaning as IRC 24(c) but the child must not have attained age 6). Nonrefundable and capped at the taxpayer's Georgia income tax liability, with no carryforward or carryback. No income phase-out: every eligible family gets the same amount regardless of income (one of only two states that do this, with Massachusetts). Part-year and nonresidents prorate by the Georgia income ratio.

name: Illinois
asOf: Tax year 2026 (35 ILCS 5/244; Illinois Department of Revenue Child Tax Credit page)
notes: Not a dollar amount per child: the credit equals 40% of the Illinois EITC (the Illinois EITC is 20% of the federal EITC, so effectively 8% of the federal EITC). Requires Illinois EITC eligibility, so the credit phases out and ends with the state EITC, not with a separate income threshold. At least one dependent child under 12 at the last day of the tax year (a qualifying child who is not a dependent also qualifies). Fully refundable; claimed on Schedule IL-E/EITC. 20% of the state EITC applied to tax years 2024 and earlier, 40% from tax year 2025 onward.

name: Maine
asOf: Tax year 2025 amounts (Maine Revenue Services Dependent Exemption Tax Credit Worksheet for tax year 2025); tax year 2026 worksheet not yet published as of 2026-07
notes: Dependent Exemption Tax Credit: $610 per qualifying child under 6 at end of tax year and $305 per qualifying dependent age 6 and older (statutory base $300, doubled for children under 6, indexed for inflation). Refundable for Maine residents and part-year residents; nonresidents get a prorated nonrefundable amount. Phase-out is $20 for each $500 of Maine AGI above $100,000 single, $125,000 head of household, $150,000 married filing jointly or surviving spouse, $75,000 married filing separately (tax year 2025 thresholds; thresholds are indexed for inflation for tax years after 2025). Press coverage in July 2026 quotes $310 and $610 for tax year 2026, but the official tax year 2026 worksheet was not published at the time of checking. L.D. 2212 (2026) keeps eligibility aligned with the federal child tax credit after the federal personal exemption was permanently repealed.

name: Maryland
asOf: Tax year 2025 (Maryland Form 502CR instructions, revision 10/25; 2026 legislation HB 363 / SB 468 adds a local county credit from tax year 2027)
notes: $500 per qualified child. A qualified child is a dependent under age 6, or a dependent over age 5 and under 17 who has a disability. No limit on the number of children. Full $500 at federal AGI of $15,000 or less; reduced by $50 for each $1,000 (or fraction) of federal AGI above $15,000; credit is zero above $24,000 (Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025 added the phase-out for tax year 2025 and later). The $15,000 and $24,000 thresholds are the same for every filing status.

name: Massachusetts
asOf: Tax year 2026 (Massachusetts Department of Revenue, Child and Family Tax Credit page updated 2026-03-11; $440 applies from tax year 2024 onward)
notes: Child and Family Tax Credit: $440 for each eligible individual - a dependent child under 13, a dependent or spouse with a disability, or a dependent age 65 or older. Refundable, no income limit and no cap on the number of dependents (one of only two states that give the same amount at every income, with Georgia). No phase-out thresholds, so maxIncome is null by design. Part-year residents are prorated; nonresidents cannot claim it; married filing separately cannot claim it. A taxpayer claims either this credit or the Dependent Care Tax Credit, not both.

name: Minnesota
asOf: Tax year 2026 (Minnesota Department of Revenue flyer revised 8/26; Minnesota House Research brief on the child credit and Working Family Credit)
notes: $1,800 per qualifying child under 18 (was $1,750 through tax year 2025; indexed for inflation), with no cap on the number of children. The child credit and the Working Family Credit are added together and phased out at 12% of income above $32,680 for unmarried filers and $38,770 for married filing jointly, so the income at which the credit reaches zero depends on the number of children: tax year 2026 fully phased out at $50,910 (unmarried) and $57,000 (joint) for one young child, $65,910 and $72,000 for two. A smaller credit applies to qualifying older children ages 18-23.

name: New Jersey
notes: Refundable credit for each child who has not attained age 6, for taxpayers with New Jersey taxable income of $80,000 or less (the limit applies to every filing status). Amounts are stepped by income, not gradual: tax years 2026-2028 give $1,250 (taxable income $30,000 or less), $1,000 ($30,001-$40,000), $750 ($40,001-$50,000), $500 ($50,001-$60,000), $250 ($60,001-$80,000). The increase is temporary: from tax year 2029 the amounts revert to $1,000 / $800 / $600 / $400 / $200. Part-year residents are prorated by months of residency.

name: New Mexico
asOf: Tax year 2025 amounts (New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department child tax credit chart; tax year 2026 PIT-RC table not yet published as of 2026-10)
notes: Child Income Tax Credit is refundable and varies by adjusted gross income: tax year 2025 amounts per qualifying child are $637 (AGI up to $25,000), $424 ($25k-$50k), $212 ($50k-$75k), $106 ($75k-$100k), $79 ($100k-$200k), $53 ($200k-$350k), $26 (above $350k). The amount for a qualifying child under 6 is double the table amount. Amounts are indexed for inflation each year, so tax year 2026 values will differ; they are published in the tax year 2026 PIT-RC instructions. The credit expires after tax year 2031.

name: New York
asOf: Tax year 2026 (A3009 (2025); New York Department of Taxation and Finance, FY2027 personal income tax expenditure estimates)
notes: Empire State Child Credit for tax years 2026 and 2027: $1,000 per qualifying child under age 4 and $500 per qualifying child age 4 through 16 (the age 4-16 amount was $330 in tax year 2025). After tax year 2027 the credit reverts to the greater of $100 per child or 33% of the pre-2017 federal child tax credit, and the income phase-in for low-income families is reinstated. Phase-out begins at federal AGI of $110,000 (married filing jointly), $75,000 (single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse) and $55,000 (married filing separately), reduced by $16.50 per $1,000 above the threshold; there is no stated income cut-off. Children must be under 17 at year end; the minimum income phase-in was removed for tax years 2025-2027.

name: Oklahoma
asOf: Tax year 2026 (26 Okl. Stat. tit. 68, sec. 2355(B)(2); Oklahoma Form 511 and Schedule 511NR instructions)
notes: The Oklahoma child care / child tax credit is the greater of 20% of the federal child and dependent care credit or 5% of the federal child tax credit (including the refundable additional child tax credit), so percentOfFederal is 5 with a second option based on the federal CDCTC. Nonrefundable. Allowed only if federal AGI is $100,000 or less - above that no credit is allowed at all - and prorated by the ratio of Oklahoma AGI to federal AGI. Eligibility follows the federal qualifying child rules, so there is no separate state age limit.

name: Oregon
asOf: Tax year 2026 (Oregon Form OR-40-FY instructions for tax year 2026)
notes: Oregon Kids Credit: $1,050 per qualifying dependent age 5 or younger at the end of the tax year, for up to five dependents. Full credit at Oregon qualifying income of $27,250 or less, reduced above that, and no credit at $32,250 or more. The same income limits apply to every filing status, and married filing separately returns are ineligible. Amounts are indexed for inflation each year (tax year 2025: $1,050, phase-out $26,550-$31,550). The credit applies to tax years 2023-2028.

name: Utah
asOf: Tax year 2026 (H.B. 290, 2026 General Session, signed 2026-03-24, effective 2026-05-06 with retrospective operation for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01)
notes: Nonrefundable $1,000 per qualifying child who is under 6 at the end of the tax year and qualifies for the federal child tax credit. H.B. 290 raised the phase-out thresholds for tax year 2026 to $49,000 (single or head of household), $61,000 (joint) and $30,500 (married filing separately). The credit is reduced by $0.10 for each dollar of modified AGI above the threshold, so it runs off quickly and there is no fixed income cut-off. Form TC-150 for tax year 2026 also caps the credit per return (for example $300 for a single taxpayer with no dependents, $600 for married filing jointly with no dependents).

name: Vermont
asOf: Tax year 2026 (Vermont Department of Taxes, Tax Credits and Adjustments for Individuals; Act 71 of 2025)
notes: $1,000 per eligible child who is six years old or younger at the close of the tax year (age limit raised from under 6 to under 7 for tax year 2025 by Act 71 of 2025). Fully refundable. Phase-out starts at AGI of $125,000 - the same threshold for single and joint filers - at $20 for every $1,000 of AGI, so the credit is fully phased out at $175,000. Part-year residents are prorated by the share of income earned while resident. SSN or ITIN not required.

name: Idaho
asOf: Tax year 2026 status (credit expired 2026-01-01; Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center, 2026 State Policy Roadmap, September 2026)
notes: NOT AVAILABLE in tax year 2026. Idaho's nonrefundable $205 per qualifying child credit was enacted for tax years 2018 through 2025 and expired on 2026-01-01; bills H. 782 and S. 1450 that would have repealed the expiration did not pass in the 2026 session. Recorded here only so the calculator can show zero for Idaho in tax year 2026.

name: District of Columbia
asOf: Tax year 2026 status (legislation repealed before taking effect; Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center, 2026 State Policy Roadmap, September 2026)
notes: NOT AVAILABLE in tax year 2026. A refundable $1,000 per child under 18 credit was enacted in December 2025 (B26-0457 and B26-0458), but Congress repealed it, so it will not take effect; the earlier $420 per child under 6 credit was repealed before it started in tax year 2025. Recorded here only so the calculator can show zero for the District of Columbia in tax year 2026.

name: Rhode Island
asOf: Tax year 2026 status (credit starts in tax year 2027; Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center, 2026 State Policy Roadmap, September 2026)
notes: NOT AVAILABLE in tax year 2026. H. 7127 (2026) creates a refundable credit of up to $330 per child age 18 and under, but it applies to tax year 2027 and later. Recorded here only so the calculator can show zero for Rhode Island in tax year 2026.
